Zolochiv Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished and overbuilt, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' Zolochiv's first Jewish settlers built a synagogue in 1613, later reconstructed after a 1727 fire; a mikvah and this cemetery both functioned by the first half of the 17th century. Unlike most communities in this collection, Zolochiv's Jewish population was not negatively affected by WWI, reaching 5,744 people (52 percent of the town) by 1921. From the start of the 1941 occupation, mass executions and a pogrom claimed thousands of lives; nearly 4,500 Jews were deported to the Bełżec extermination camp in late 1942, and the ghetto's liquidation in April 1943 saw 3,500 more shot. This, the older of Zolochiv's two Jewish cemeteries, is by all other accounts a car park today.
